lore_anchors.definition: A rare, high-grade spirit insect that produces durable golden threads capable of binding magical treasures and even shaking ancient artifacts; in the Mortal Stream, possessing one signals elite-level resource access.
An ancient, powerful aquatic spirit beast (a type of flood dragon) associated with extreme yin-cold energy; it serves as a symbol of its owner’s high status and formidable combat power.
A translucent, ancient spirit tortoise revered for its defensive capabilities; its name derives from classical Chinese mythology where tortoises are symbols of longevity and divination.
The supreme treasure sealed at the innermost heart of the Void Heaven Palace; the primary objective of the expedition and the source of the blinding blue light.
A tiered ranking of spirit insects in the cultivation world, functioning as a survival manual for cultivators who know which bugs to fear and which to capture.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the Golden Silk Silkworm and why is it important here?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It's a rare spirit insect whose golden threads are strong enough to tug on an ancient artifact like the Void Heaven Cauldron; Wan Tianming using several at once signals a major resource escalation the demonic side didn't anticipate.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why did Man Brutal Beard attack immediately?
cultural_notes_faq.a: To seize the initiative—if he let Wan Tianming finish pulling out the cauldron, the fight would happen on the righteous path's terms; attacking early forces a reaction and disrupts their timing.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is a Daoist Name / Dao Hao?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It's a title cultivators adopt (like 'Qing Yi Jushi') that reflects their personal philosophy or specialty; elders switching between names mid-chapter reinforces their layered identity and political positioning.
